title: Country Gospel
style: Classic Country, 1960s female vocal, storytelling, honky tonk, acoustic guitar, piano, fiddle, steel guitar, simple drums, warm analog production
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Storm signs rising
Red in the sky
Fig tree budding
Branches getting high
Wars and rumors
Running through the land
Nation against nation
Trouble like the sand

False ones talking
Calling out Your name
Sheep hearts shaking
Chasing smoke and flame
Birth pains breaking
Closer every hour
Every cracked foundation tasting fire and power

[Chorus]
Watch and pray
Child
Watch and pray
Like the Good Book said
There’ll come a day
Heaven and earth gonna roll away
But His word still stands
So watch and pray

[Verse 2]
They’ll say
“Lo here
” they’ll say
“Lo there”
Wolf-teeth smiling
Dressed up like they care
In the secret chambers
Out in the field
Chasing every whisper
Every shiny seal

Lightning flashes
East to the west
So the Son of Man comes
Shining on the rest
Carcass lying
Vultures in the air
Gathered in a moment
Judgment everywhere

[Chorus]

[Verse 3]
Days of old Noah
Folks eating fine
Drinking at the table
Laughing at the sign
Taking and giving
Brides in a white dress
Never see the waters climbing up their chest

Door swung shut when the first drops fell
Too late knocking on that wood-lined shell
Two out working
Walking in the sun
One heart taken
Other one left undone

[Chorus]

[Verse 4]
Sun gone dark and the moon turns dim
Powers of the heaven start to lose their limb
Stars fall staggering
Shaking in the sky
Every proud mountain learning how to cry

Trumpet sounding
Clouds gonna part
All the tribes mourning deep inside the heart
Angels gathering from the four strong winds
From one far end to the other end again

[Chorus]

[Bridge]
[low vocal register]
Like a thief in the night
He comes
When the porch light’s low and the hound dog hums
If the house man knew when that hour would break
He’d sit up waiting
He’d never sleep late

So who’s the faithful servant
Who’s the lazy hand?
Feeding in the season like the Master planned
Blessed that worker when the Lord steps in
Catches him ready
Working through the din

[Chorus]
